decisions.title: Write the plan and docs before the code
Stack: Turborepo, NestJS API, Next.js app, Prisma with pgvector, BullMQ
decisions.why: One TypeScript codebase with shared types.

decisions.title: Own email/password JWT auth instead of the documented Clerk with MFA
decisions.why: Faster to ship; docs and code still disagree, MFA not built.

decisions.title: Withdrew the claim that no competitor has prep and cross-session memory
decisions.why: Upheal, Mentalyc and SimplePractice advertise cross-session features.

decisions.title: Removed unsourced time-saved statistics and "HIPAA-ready" / signed-BAA claims
decisions.why: No supporting source; no BAAs executed.

decisions.title: Solo plan capped at 200 AI notes per month with a 30-day trial
decisions.why: Founder accepted the recommendation; to be tested against $19 / $29 / $39 on the waitlist.

decisions.title: Parse note drafts as JSON first, with labelled-prose fallback
decisions.why: The live model returns fenced JSON; the old parser showed raw JSON.

decisions.title: Restyle the app and docs on a calm light palette
decisions.why: Contrast failures (2.84:1 and 3.06:1) and a flat dark theme.

decisions.title: First segment: US independent therapists already using AI; India deferred
decisions.why: Reachable, price-sensitive, clear workflow; India pool small and uncountable. Not yet confirmed by the founder.

decisions.title: Patient-facing activity loop is a gated pilot, not an MVP feature
decisions.why: Differentiation candidate but adds PHI surface and state-law risk.

decisions.title: Build a discovery and pilot-recruitment deck now; defer the investor deck
decisions.why: No traction, validation or compliance evidence yet.

decisions.title: Position on inspectable memory and a strict no-retention posture, not on price or "AI notes"
decisions.why: AI notes and the $29 price are not differentiators.

decisions.title: Obtain counsel opinion before any patient-facing release
decisions.why: Nevada scope, psychotherapy-notes status of reflections, information blocking.

decisions.title: Pseudonymise names before AI calls and pursue zero-retention endpoints before any pilot

bets.name: Source-linked, editable patient memory
bets.problem: Therapists distrust AI summaries and re-read old notes.
bets.hypothesis: Clinicians will click through to sources and trust the brief more.
bets.action: Add a source-reference table and link every summary line to its note.
bets.metric: ≥50% of weekly users open a source link at least weekly

bets.name: Clinician-approved activity loop
bets.problem: Homework is ad hoc and rarely reviewed.
bets.hypothesis: Clinicians want session-grounded activities with patient reflections feeding the next prep brief.
bets.action: Clickable prototype first; gated pilot only after counsel opinion and BAA path.
bets.metric: ≥40% activities opened; clinicians review reflections for ≥60% of cases

bets.name: Copy-to-EHR export with strict no-retention posture
bets.problem: Notes must live in the EHR; fear of recorded transcripts.
bets.hypothesis: Text-first plus no retention moves buying decisions.
bets.action: Per-EHR formatted copy; publish data-flow; pseudonymise before model calls.
bets.threshold: Privacy cited by <3 of 10 conversion interviews: reposition
